instructions.quote:
Each surface should declare exactly ONE primary action (most
   prominent button, brightest accent). Multiple peer-level
   primaries → `HIERARCHY_TIE`.

Information density: count interactive elements per surface;
   flag >9 peer-level CTAs as `INTERACTION_OVERLOAD`.

Inline `color:` + `background-color:` pairs computed at <3.0
   ratio → `OBVIOUS_CONTRAST_FAIL` HIGH. Defer subtler AA cases
   to the accessibility-reviewer.

Spacing tokens: every margin/padding must resolve to a token
   in the declared design system. Magic numbers → `OFF_GRID`.

Type rhythm: line-height should resolve to a multiple of the
   base unit (typically 4px or 8px). Off-rhythm → `RHYTHM_BREAK`.

This is not the accessibility-reviewer (that has narrower WCAG focus)
and not the ui-auditor (that runs late in the pipeline against the
implemented surface). The design-critic fires earlier, on the design
artefact, before code is written.

Static mockups referenced by path (don't open images; read the
     filename and any sibling spec markdown).

Do not grade aesthetics in the abstract — every finding must trace
to a stated rule (hierarchy, rhythm, contrast, intent).

A pixel-perfect implementation of a weak
design is still a weak design.

Do not invent design-system tokens — only validate against what
the brief declares.

notes: A read-only, rule-traceable pre-implementation design-critique gate with an explicit finding taxonomy (HIERARCHY_TIE, OFF_GRID, RHYTHM_BREAK, etc.), a strict boundary against duplicating a separate accessibility-reviewer and a later ui-auditor, and an explicit refusal to open images (works from filenames/specs/tokens only).

instructions.quote: Never animate keyboard-initiated actions. These actions are repeated hundreds of times daily.

Only animate transform and opacity. These properties skip layout and paint, running on the GPU.
If velocity exceeds ~0.11, dismiss regardless of distance. A quick flick should be enough.

**`in oklab`** is the best default: even brightness, no hue surprises.
Measure a foreground against the background it actually renders on, not the page background.

Never `Approve` coverage you did not inspect.

Outer radius = inner radius + padding. Mismatched radii on nested elements is the most common thing that makes an interface feel off.

An icon next to text carries the text's optical weight: `1.5px` stroke beside regular (400) text, `2px` beside semibold (600).
